ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — John F. Kennedy

code.originalText: Nine-month review: replacement, thyroid, autoimmune screening, bone health, and back pain

text.paragraph: Nine-month review: replacement, thyroid, autoimmune screening, bone health, and back pain. [S]

Mr. Kennedy returns nine months after his first visit. He feels well and works full days. He takes hydrocortisone 10, 5 and 5 mg, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg and levothyroxine 50 mcg without missed doses. He has had no illness needing stress doses since the influenza in the winter, and he carries his kit and wears his medical ID. He has no salt craving, lightheadedness, palpitations or cold intolerance. His back is stiff after long flights but no longer limits him, and he swims most days. His mood is good. [S]

list.item: No adrenal crisis and no emergency admission through nine months. Outcome by 2026-10-19: No crisis or admission; one febrile illness managed at home with stress dosing [S]

Hydrocortisone at the lowest dose that keeps him well, within 15 to 25 mg a day, with his weight back toward his usual 72 kg and no signs of over-replacement. Outcome by 2026-10-19: Hydrocortisone 20 mg a day in three doses; weight 72.0 kg from 66.0; no signs of excess [S]

Sodium and potassium normal, renin in the upper normal range, and no postural drop in blood pressure by the six-week review. Outcome by 2026-03-09: Sodium 139, potassium 4.4 mmol/L; renin 2.6 ng/mL/h; no postural drop [S]
He can state the sick-day rules and give the emergency injection by the two-week visit. Outcome by 2026-01-26: Stated the rules and gave a practice injection on a trainer [S]
Oswestry Disability Index below 20% by three months, with the brace used only for long travel. Outcome by 2026-04-20: Oswestry 18% at three months; brace used only on long journeys [S]
